Hereditary amyloid protein deposition prominently affects kidneys, with gastrointestinal dysfunction sufficiently common to qualify. Hepatic deposition alone does not establish common functional damage.
Bladder and rectal descent are common anatomical components of pelvic organ prolapse, supporting renal and gastrointestinal primary labels independently of urinary or bowel symptoms.
Infection defines this umbrella; extrapulmonary sites vary. Pulmonary involvement cannot be inherited automatically from the broader tuberculosis parent.
Dysferlinopathy is a skeletal muscle disease. Its neurological ancestry does not establish direct brain, spinal cord or peripheral nerve damage.
Corneal thinning and associated astigmatism define an ocular disorder; no additional axis is supported.
The definition explicitly establishes skin as the tumor site. Neural differentiation and broad neoplasm ancestry do not require an additional neurologic label.
Hibernoma usually occupies subcutaneous adipose tissue, supporting dermatologic primary. Uncommon intramuscular or central nervous system sites do not define the umbrella.

Developmental impairment, skeletal abnormalities and heart defects define the syndrome. Oral structural defects occur in 30–79%, supporting gastrointestinal involvement; the four-axis cap explains omission of urethral anomalies.
